result.summary: The environment is highly hostile to pedestrians, lacking any dedicated walking infrastructure such as sidewalks or marked crossings. Pedestrians are forced onto an unpaved shoulder that is further obstructed by parked vehicles, necessitating movement into the active travel lane.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Infrastructure
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk or paved walkway, forcing pedestrians to walk on a dirt shoulder or in the roadway.

hazards.name: Obstruction on Shoulder
hazards.description: A parked vehicle occupies the dirt shoulder, forcing any pedestrian to enter the travel lane to pass.

interventions.title: Construct Sidewalks
interventions.description: Install a paved, ADA-compliant sidewalk separated from the roadway to provide a safe space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Install Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add overhead street lighting to improve visibility for pedestrians and drivers during low-light conditions.

interventions.title: Implement Parking Restrictions
interventions.description: Prohibit parking on the shoulder to ensure the path remains clear for pedestrians where sidewalks are absent.

result.summary: The environment features a continuous sidewalk but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or ADA-compliant curb ramps at the intersection. A large brick building situated directly at the property line creates a blind corner, obstructing sightlines between pedestrians and vehicles turning from the side street.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians or to define a safe crossing path.

hazards.name: Blind Corner
hazards.description: The building's placement at the corner limits visibility for drivers approaching the stop sign and pedestrians walking along the main sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the building meets the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The absence of sloped curb transitions makes the intersection inaccessible for people using wheelchairs or other mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk in the foreground

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to increase driver awareness and define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at the corner to ensure the pedestrian network is accessible to all users.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the corner to improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses and sidewalks on both sides, but lacks marked crosswalks or traffic control at the visible intersection. The wide roadway and lack of pedestrian-specific infrastructure increase exposure and potential vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, making pedestrian movements unpredictable for drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to regulate vehicle flow at this wide intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Control
interventions.description: Install stop signs to manage traffic flow and reduce speeds through the residential area.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of dedicated crossing infrastructure and narrow, poorly maintained sidewalks. The industrial setting with chain-link fences and parked vehicles creates a hostile environment for walking with no protected space for pedestrians to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked locations for pedestrians to cross the two-lane roadway safely.

hazards.name: Narrow and obstructed sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right is narrow and constrained by a chain-link fence, which may force pedestrians closer to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the road along the fence line.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and vegetation along the roadside can block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway where cars are parked.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility (continental style) marked crosswalks to provide designated crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Repair
interventions.description: Widen the existing sidewalk and repair cracked surfaces to ensure a continuous, accessible path of travel.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.
